# The Blyx handbook

Blyx 0.2.1 · Released language and toolchain

Start with a complete fn main(). Run your program in the playground or use blyxc check FILE followed by blyxc run FILE. For a native executable, use blyxc build FILE with Rust and a host linker installed.

[Learn Blyx](https://www.blyx-lang.space/learn) · [Playground](https://www.blyx-lang.space/play) · [Executable subset](https://github.com/Rahulchaube1/blyxxxx/blob/blyx-main/docs/executable-subset.md) · [Full handbook](https://doc.blyx-lang.space/llms-full.txt)

The release supports synchronous functions, recursion, control flow and numeric vectors. Native projects can import Git-pinned Blyx packages and read files or command-line arguments. See the [ecosystem](https://www.blyx-lang.space/packages) for published libraries. GPU kernels, async tasks and a general tensor runtime are under development.

## First steps

- [Your first Blyx program](https://doc.blyx-lang.space/guide/first-program) — Start in the browser, make a prediction, then edit and run your first line of Blyx.

- [Numbers and expressions](https://doc.blyx-lang.space/guide/arithmetic) — Use a packing problem to learn whole numbers, decimals, operator order and integer division.

- [Text, comments and output](https://doc.blyx-lang.space/guide/text-output) — Build a receipt one value at a time and learn how strings differ from variable names.

## Language essentials

- [Bindings, mutation and scope](https://doc.blyx-lang.space/guide/bindings) — Trace a name through nested blocks and choose when a value should change.

- [Booleans and decisions](https://doc.blyx-lang.space/guide/decisions) — Classify temperatures, then test exactly what happens at the boundaries.

- [Functions, parameters and results](https://doc.blyx-lang.space/guide/functions) — Give a calculation a name, call it more than once, and use its return value in another expression.

- [While loops and the Euclidean algorithm](https://doc.blyx-lang.space/guide/control-flow) — Trace changing state and explain why a loop finishes.

- [Break, continue and loop values](https://doc.blyx-lang.space/guide/loop-exits) — Find the first matching integer and carry it out of a loop.

- [Recursion and the cost of a call](https://doc.blyx-lang.space/guide/recursion) — Trace Fibonacci by hand, identify the base case, and decide when iteration is cheaper.

## Numerical programming

- [Vectors and reductions](https://doc.blyx-lang.space/guide/vectors) — Represent several readings in one value and combine them into a weighted mean.

- [Scan a vector for its maximum](https://doc.blyx-lang.space/guide/vector-scans) — Design a loop that finds the largest value even when every reading is negative.

- [Smooth a sequence with one running value](https://doc.blyx-lang.space/guide/smoothing) — Turn a noisy signal into a sequence of estimates and trace how much history each estimate retains.

- [Fit a line and predict a value](https://doc.blyx-lang.space/guide/numerical-models) — Fit a one-parameter model, inspect its assumptions, and predict the response at an unseen input.

- [Measure prediction error](https://doc.blyx-lang.space/guide/model-error) — Evaluate a set of predictions, trace the residuals and interpret their mean squared error.

- [Classify using a score and a threshold](https://doc.blyx-lang.space/guide/classification) — Combine two features, choose a category, and decide how ties are classified.

## Practical projects

- [Test a program at its boundaries](https://doc.blyx-lang.space/guide/testing) — Design a small repeatable test suite that catches an off-by-one classification rule.

- [Capstone project — build a sensor report](https://doc.blyx-lang.space/guide/sensor-report) — Build a complete report from a blank file, handle empty input, and verify a boundary condition.

- [Evaluate models with Blyx packages](https://doc.blyx-lang.space/guide/ai-packages) — Compare the cost of two classifiers, check their probability forecasts, and score a ranked retrieval result. Run the comparison in CI or import the same Blyx functions into your application.

- [Train, calibrate and monitor a regression model](https://doc.blyx-lang.space/guide/training-and-monitoring) — Fit a regression, attach intervals using held-out errors, and catch persistent underprediction in a later stream. Run each stage in native Blyx or the browser.

## Local toolchain

- [Install and verify Blyx](https://doc.blyx-lang.space/guide/installation) — Choose a binary or package manager, locate the executable, and verify the exact compiler version.

- [Create a project on disk](https://doc.blyx-lang.space/guide/projects) — Move a program from the browser into a project, check the file and run it from a terminal.

- [Develop in VS Code](https://doc.blyx-lang.space/guide/editor) — Run an unsaved editor buffer, read a parser diagnostic and move the same program to the CLI.

- [Debug and recover from errors](https://doc.blyx-lang.space/guide/diagnostics) — Locate a syntax error, diagnose a runtime failure, and guard an operation using short-circuit evaluation.

- [Build a native executable](https://doc.blyx-lang.space/guide/native-builds) — Compile a typed Blyx program and compare the executable with the interpreter on the same input.

## Language reference

- [Syntax, types and operators](https://doc.blyx-lang.space/guide/language-reference) — Look up the executable forms, operator order and value types used in Blyx 0.2.1.

- [Built-in functions and output](https://doc.blyx-lang.space/guide/builtin-reference) — Look up every vector built-in and both output macros, including their inputs, results and boundary cases.

- [Command-line reference](https://doc.blyx-lang.space/guide/cli-reference) — Look up CLI forms, output files, execution budgets and exit codes.

- [What Blyx 0.2.1 can run](https://doc.blyx-lang.space/guide/compatibility) — Choose an execution mode and identify features that are still being developed.
